name: mafft
desc: Multiple alignments with fast Fourier transforms
why: Fast Fourier transform applied to multiple sequence alignment is real bioinformatics worth a look, though it's a known specialist tool.

brief.what_it_is: MAFFT is a multiple sequence alignment program for unix-like operating systems. You give it a FASTA file of amino acid or nucleotide sequences, and it writes an alignment to standard output. It recognizes whether the input is protein or nucleotide automatically. It offers several strategies, from L-INS-i, which is accurate for up to about 200 sequences, to FFT-NS-2, which is fast enough for up to about 30,000 sequences.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as a multiple sequence alignment program and presents its strategies as trade-offs between accuracy and speed on large datasets. The 2002 paper it cites is titled 'MAFFT: a novel method for rapid multiple sequence alignment based on fast Fourier transform'. The README does not give a broader problem statement beyond this.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage names the fast Fourier transform as the basis of the method, in the title of the 2002 paper it cites, and mentions a PartTree algorithm for building an approximate tree from a large number of unaligned sequences. The page does not explain the mechanism in detail, so the FFT's role in the alignment step should be described only at that level.

commands_seen.context: General form of the command. Input is a FASTA file, output is redirected to a file.
Alias for the accurate L-INS-i option, for alignments of up to about 200 sequences by about 2,000 sites.
Runs the fast FFT-NS-2 option, intended for larger alignments.
Suggested when unsure which option to use; MAFFT chooses the strategy.

brief.install_notes: The homepage has download sections for Mac OS X, Linux, Windows and Source, but the page gives no URLs for them, so the writer should not invent one. The README gives no account, runtime or first-run configuration. Beyond brew install, no extra setup is described on the homepage.
brief.standout: A single program covers a range of accuracy and speed trade-offs, and its --auto mode picks one for you. It also detects protein versus nucleotide input without being told which.
brief.status: Probably maintained. The homepage says the latest version is 7.526 (2024/Apr), and it warns about a bug in versions 7.463 to 7.486 that was fixed in 7.487 (2021/Jul/25). The contact email has been 'temporarily unavailable since 2018/Feb/7', and the page links a manual labelled v6.240, so parts of the documentation look older than the release.
brief.caveats: Runs on unix-like operating systems per the homepage. The license depends on the package: mafft-*-without-extensions-src.tgz is BSD, while the Windows zip is GPL. Bundled packages (Vienna RNA, MXSCARNA, ProbConsRNA) for RNA structural alignment carry their own licenses. Versions 7.463 to 7.486 have a memory bug in the FFT-NS-i option and in --auto, so use 7.487 or later. The listed contact email is out of date, and the manual is v6.240. The brew caveats field was empty.
